_: The army layer (docs/research/army-layer-2026-11-12.md). The massed army (scripts/army.gd, scripts/army_vat.gdshader, scripts/army_banner.gdshader read it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). The host is commanded by regiment (Total War; docs/research/army-and-town-rules.md section 1): each regiment one VAT draw, one banner. units: the kinds of regiment, by name: role (melee stands in the front line, ranged behind it, cavalry on the wings), glyph on its banner (sword, spear, bow, horse, axe, engine), share of a host made up from a head count, men in one regiment, asset (the baked soldier's folder under res://assets/, tools/rig/README.md), freeciv (the Freeciv unit types that raise it; one regiment per company of the bridge's hosts), spacing (file, rank: units between men abreast and front to back; cavalry stands looser), speed (share of march.speed; a host marches at its slowest), and any of a mesh's fields to override them. meshes: per baked soldier folder: albedo (its paint, albedo.png for image-made units), team (rects: the palette cells in team.rects take the house colour, the KayKit way; mask: mask.png's white takes it, the rig pipeline's way), tracks (its baked clips by role: idle, walk, ready, attack, hit, death; rest is the pool men at ease play, name: weight). fallbackUnit: the kind a company of an unknown Freeciv type raises. man: the soldier's height in world units (the realm's people stand ~0.22). jitter.place, jitter.turn, jitter.size: how far a man stands off his mark, turns off the line (radians), and differs in size (share); jitter.rank: how far a rank bows forward or back along its length; jitter.step: how far a marching man is off his regiment's step (share of a stride). gap: units between regiments. column.files: men abreast on the march, low and high (8-10: 03-army's blocks; 4-6 strung a regiment of 56 figures out 14 ranks deep, pass g2's host5); column.fileMost: units between men abreast on the march, at most, for men on foot (a man is about 0.055 wide; at 0.12-0.18 g7/g8's host5 read loose); column.footRankMost: units between their ranks on the march, at most; column.rank: units between ranks on the march, at least; column.rankMost: at most (horse, whose line spacing is 0.5, closes up on the march); column.gap: units between regiments nose to tail; column.order: roles front to back. line.frontage: men abreast in the line, by role, low and high; line.maxFront: regiments abreast in one row before another row forms behind; line.rowGap: units between rows; line.wingGap: units between the front row and its cavalry wings; line.reform: seconds a regiment takes to turn from column to line. march.speed: units a second; march.lead: units the column's head marches along the road before it reaches the muster; march.roadTries: how many nearby towns are asked for a road in. march.form: seconds a host raised for war (the muster scene) stands formed at its seat before it marches out; march.linger: seconds it stands in column at the road's end before it is gone (the map's companies carry on); march.men: the men a muster raises when the crown has no host in the field, or for a house's rising. march.roadReach: how far off the road a muster's field may lie and its host still march out along the road (it walks onto it first; the realm's roads.reach is for everyone else). rest.every: seconds between a regiment's men shifting at ease, low and high; rest.men: how many shift each time, low and high; rest.turn: radians a man turns as he shifts. deck: a host aboard ship (army.gd board; 08-reinforce): files, men abreast in a regiment's block on the deck; length, units of a hull's deck its regiments share out along; y_m, the deck's height in metres over the hull's base as units.gd sinks it; file, seconds between regiments filing down to the hulls. muster.cell: units to a cell of the field search; muster.clear: units kept clear round the seat's centre; muster.wayReach: how far past the town's edge (units; a tile is 4) war's muster looks along each main way out for a stretch clear for its column; muster.roadClear: units of clear ground either side of war's muster column on the road (no building, hedge, field or cottage; army.gd _form_on_way); muster.gateClear: units past the town's edge (where the way out leaves it, at the wall's gate) where war's muster column has its tail (army.gd _form_on_way); muster.reach: how far out the field may run; muster.slope: the most a cell's ground may rise across it; muster.keepOff: no road or track within this share of a cell's width; muster.treeCost: what a tree on the line's ground costs; muster.missCost: what a cell of the line on unsuitable ground costs; muster.nearCost: what a cell further from the seat costs. banner.height: a regiment's banner pole in men's heights; banner.width: its cloth's reach in men's heights; banner.fixedFrom: camera distance beyond which banners keep their size on screen; banner.pips: strength pips under the flag. banner.bearer: how far to his right (men's heights) the front rank's middle man carries it. standard.scale: the army's standard against a regiment's banner. select.margin: units the ground rectangle reaches past a regiment; select.alpha: the rectangle's strength when selected; select.idle: its strength when not (0 hides it). far.at: camera distance beyond which the host shows as coloured blocks with its standard; far.back: the distance it turns back to men (no flicker in between). colours: crown (every regiment in the crown's colour, the art target's one-colour host) or houses (each regiment its house's, levies). spike.strength: in the spike only, the made-up regiments' strength, low and high (a real host's comes from its companies' hit points over hpFull). camera.pitch: degrees down the army shot's lens looks (03-army's, about 38; camera_rig.tilt_for; the battle's lens too); camera.quarter: radians the lens stands off the line's front; camera.marchQuarter: off the column's heading; camera.musterOff: radians war's muster lens stands off straight behind its column, looking down it; camera.musterHold: the muster lens at least this share of the column's length away, so every block is in frame. albedo: the paint's brightness under the realm's sun. team.rects: up to four KayKit palette cells (u0, v0, u1, v1, and how much of it takes the colour) that wear the house colour; team.shade: the colour's brightness over the cloth's own light. team.mask_edge: how much of a mask.png texel's white makes it all cloth (low, high; far off the mask's mipmaps average cloth with the white around it, and a half-dyed cloth read pink). emblem.on: whether regiments wear their house's arms (the top of its banner, assets/heraldry) on the shield's face and the tabard's front; emblem.rect: where the arms sit in the banner picture (u0, v0, u1, v1); emblem.light: their paint's brightness under the sun. meshes.<dir>.emblem: up to two places on that soldier, in his rest pose (tools/emblem_probe.gd measures the pieces): center, size (across, up, depth), facing and up, facingMin (how square its face must turn to the facing), round (a roundel, for a round shield). look: the painted finish every soldier wears: steel found by saturation under steelSat, its metal, roughness, paint lift and faint glow; the rim light and its tint; the darkening toward the feet (footDark the soles' value, fading up through footHeight of his height); the cloth's trim band's value (trimDark); each man's variation in value and tint (varyValue, varyTint). meshes.<dir>.trim: up to two bands of the rest pose's height (share, low and high) where the house cloth is trim. Each kind wears its own baked soldier (units.<kind>.asset): the Meshy men-at-arms, the town guard as spearmen, the ranger as archers, armies/cavalry for horse; the Meshy knight armies/meshy_knight (docs/art/army, 14 sword-and-shield clips) for knights and, until the engines have their own models, their crews. A role's clips: one name, a list (each man picks one), or name: weight (a pool; rarer clips lighter). The Meshy soldiers' cloth takes the house colour by its own hue (tools/rig/rig.json units.<stem>.mask). muster.margin: units of clear ground a regiment keeps round its rectangle; muster.probe: units between the points its ground is tested at; muster.search: how far (units) a regiment whose place falls on a house, a farm, a hedged field or a road looks for clear ground (army.gd _clear_slots). lod: the soldiers' lighter levels (Godot's own generated detail levels over the same vertices, so the baked motion holds; --army-lod=off for the before): on, bias (higher keeps more detail further out), least (no level under this many triangles), mergeAngle. shadows.near: only regiments within this many units of the lens cast shadows (0: all). meshes.<dir>.body: the man's own height in the model's units where a carried prop stands above him (the pikeman's upright pike; the model's height otherwise). meshes.<dir>.tall: that body's height in world units, over man (a horse and its rider stand taller). armies/cavalry: one Meshy model of the knight on his barded warhorse, fitted to the CC0 horse rig (tools/rig/cavalry.json, docs/art/army); its gaits stand in for every role (idle, walk, trot, canter, gallop; no fall of its own yet). units.knights: the Meshy knight on foot.
_drawPerMan: drawPerMan: one drawn soldier for this many men (0.1: one for ten; army.gd figures, Mac 12 Nov: 'reduce the soldiers to 1/10th'). Every regiment's figures come from it (the muster, field battles, the storm); its men, the number the player reads, stay its full strength; losses drop figures in step with its men (army_field.gd _fell). figureFloor: the figures every regiment draws before its one for ten, so each reads as a formed block (supervisor 12 Nov, after GoC's muster frames); figureBudget: the most figures the realm's biggest host may draw (6,000 figures ran 23-36 fps in batch 8, half of it against the 10 fps bar; army_probe 24).
_morale: Panic spreads (army_morale.gd; the casebook's War and sieges, Bannerlord's morale after Towton): a regiment's nerve on its mind's blackboard, 1 steady .. 0 gone. start: its nerve at the start. own: how hard its own fallen shake it, by the share of it they were (losing a quarter takes 0.35). Every reach is open ground (game units) between regiments' edges, their widths along the line, so it holds however wide a battle's regiments stand. near: men of its side falling within reach shake it per_man each, less with distance. rout: a regiment of its side breaking within seen shakes it by shock, less with distance. flight: each running regiment of its side within near.reach shakes it this much a second. steady: with its side's commander within reach every shake reaches it less by share (it breaks later, never never); with nothing shaking it for after seconds it calms by rally a second. spent: once the day is spent (battle.json field.longest) the beaten side's nerve drains this much a second, so the most shaken breaks first and its break carries the rest. break: below this a regiment of the beaten side breaks. floor_victor: the victors' nerve never falls below it (Freeciv decided the day). waver_from: its banner starts to waver below this.
_spacing: spacing: game units between men (a man stands man 0.22, about 1.75 m): file, centre to centre along a rank (0.12, about 0.95 m: shoulder room); rank, between ranks (0.22, a step, about 1.75 m). A kind's own in units.<kind>.spacing: archers looser (0.18 / 0.26, about 1.4 / 2 m), horse 0.19 (1.5 m) by 0.5, engines 0.25 / 0.3. tools/army_probe.gd asserts no two men of a formation stand closer than 0.8 of their file.

minds._: Every mind in the army layer (scripts/army_mind.gd builds a LimboHSM from a row): states (each: enter, tick, exit, the fight's methods it runs on entering, each frame and on leaving; guard, the method that says whether it may be entered), go (from, to, event), any (event: the state it leads to from any other), start. A man's minds run on army_melee.gd's stagings (army_skirmish.gd: line_soldier, knight; army_assault.gd: assault_man, gap_holder), a regiment's on army_field.gd (regiment, storm_regiment).

steer._: A fighter steering toward a moving mark (mover.gd toward): lapse, seconds unasked before he stands (his mind moved on, or he fell); reroute, seconds between asking the fight's ground afresh for a way to a mark that keeps moving.

map._: The companies on the map (units.gd): march_speed, world units a second of a company's figure's steady march (a figure that must go faster to reach its tile within the season runs: units.gd march_pace); wounded_hp, hit points at or under which a company looks wounded; ship_sink, metres a ship's cog (assets/meshy/cog) sits below its foot, to its waterline.
